chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about the bleacher who spoils. He said: 'Every hired person who is given a wage on the condition that he repairs [the work], and he spoils it, then he is liable [for the loss].'

key_terms.الْقَصَّارِ: The bleacher (one who cleans and softens wool/cloth)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling if a hired worker spoils the item they were paid to repair or process?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal principle of *daman* (liability) in *ujrah* (hiring) contracts, establishing that a worker bears financial responsibility for negligence or defect in their work. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that wages are contingent upon the preservation of the entrusted item, linking commercial ethics directly to contractual fidelity.
